title: Blackened Mahi-Mahi with Lemon Butter Sauce
description: Thermapen-pulled mahi in small oval cast iron pans with a thick lemon-garlic butter sauce that clings.

steps.title: Dry the fish
steps.text: Pat {fish} completely dry with paper towels on both sides. A dry surface builds a crust instead of steaming.

steps.title: Rest at room temp
steps.text: Let the fillets sit on the counter for 10 minutes while you mix the seasoning. This takes the chill off so the centers cook evenly.

steps.title: Mix the seasoning
steps.text: On a plate, stir together {paprika}, {garlicg}, {onion}, {salt}, {pepper}, {thyme}, {oregano} and {cayenne}. This is mild-to-medium heat; add extra cayenne to your own fillet at the table if you want more.
Melt {butterdip} in a small shallow bowl in the microwave, about 30 seconds.

steps.title: Coat the fillets
steps.text: Dip each fillet in the melted butter, then press all sides into the seasoning until fully coated. Butter makes the spice stick and darken into the crust.

steps.title: Heat the pans
steps.text: Set the two small oval cast iron pans over medium-high heat with the vent fan on high. Heat 4 to 5 minutes until the pans just begin to smoke. This will smoke; the Bighorn with the same pans keeps it outside.
Add {oil} to the pans, split between them, and swirl to coat. Oil carries the heat; the butter on the fish alone would scorch.

steps.title: Sear side one
steps.text: Lay one fillet in each pan, presentation side down. Sear 2 to 3 minutes without moving until a dark crust forms.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Flip the fillets and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until the Thermapen reads 135°F in the thickest part. Pull at 135°F; mahi goes dry quickly past that.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Move the fillets to a plate and rest 2 minutes. Carryover lifts them a few degrees; leave Cindy's fillet resting a bit longer to land closer to 140°F.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: While the fish rests, melt {sbutter} in the 10 inch ear-handle skillet over medium heat. Use a clean pan, not the blackening pans.
Add {mgarlic} and stir 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in {broth} and {lemon}. Simmer 2 minutes to concentrate.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk {cornstarch} with {water} in a small cup, pour into the simmering sauce, and stir 30 to 60 seconds until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir in {parsley} and spoon the sauce generously over the fillets right before serving.

notes: Mahi dries out fast past 140°F, so trust the Thermapen over the clock. Fillets thinner than 3/4 inch need about 1.5 to 2 minutes per side. Mix a double or triple batch of the seasoning and keep it in a jar. The sauce reheats well, but the fish is best fresh. Sides that catch the sauce: Tiger rice cooker rice with Better Than Bouillon and butter, or Impastable pasta.
